title: What do you want me to build you for free (and must remain open source)
author: sheehyct
selftext:
The more time i've spent developing strategies that try to take advantage of the minuscule inefficiencies that i can identify, i've realized i have slowly racked up a decent "little" list of niche tools or applications that i make just for myself. 

Everything I develop is based off the fact of working 24-hour  shifts at the firehouse, being up all night, and coming home to two young kiddos. whatever i do, it has to make my life easy and it has to work. it has to work well and quickly. 

the kiddo's life was what got me into algo trading to begin with as i realized i was not going to have time in my manual trading. my preference would never take precedent over them. 

i have my algo. i build whatever tool or application i feel is needed to streamline how i trade, which is standard options, perpetuals, equity, and crypto via hyperliquid. for fun when i get really busy, i'll hit my prop firm account with my funded futures, honestly just because it's easier sometimes. 

a lot of things i've been making these days kind of focus on people who trade awkward hours, don't sleep a lot, are busy in life, but still when they're able, want to do the thing they enjoy (which for me is trading because i'm good at it and i like it). 

if there was something that you wanted built for free for everyone else to use as well and i'd make it for you, what would it be? why would i do this? first i'm extremely adhd. that can harness my hyperfixation superpower when the task fits. if your task does not fit, i apologize in advance. 

i'll start with my pain points and where it went. i started on hyperliquid when i stopped having as much time to trade options because trading rth hours got impossible for a while.

vpn to whatever wallet you use (unless you want to be someone who pays an immense amount of fees to something like hyperdash for builders' fees, which i would never do) is not very efficient when it comes to wanting to even simply close a position quickly or get alerts on your phone from equity or crypto perps.

trading view has helped with that if you have a subscription since they added xyz products but not everybody has that. everything out on the play store was trash at the time so i wanted everything from hyperliquid to hit my scanner on my phone app and go to my watch (samsung galaxy s26 ultra / samsung galaxy watch ultra 2 ). 

i get the alerts about what pops off, what it does price action-wise, and when i'm busy on the go and i don't have time to look, i just use biometrics and close the position. 

want to trade options, perpetuals, and maybe whatever prop firm you use as long as they support an api in one place where you don't have to bounce around with eight monitors. well yeah me too. that one's almost done. 

gth options are recently now a thing too. paying for options data is stupid expensive especially if you already have an account like schwab or tasty trade. just use their api and make your own stuff.

when you wake up at (i don't know) 2 am because you can't sleep, or 7:30 hits and stuff's popping off, you see a stupid wide spread on a single-stock equity option. you want to calculate the optimal entry point for that premium while you're walking your dog, your kid is actively likely pooping on you, and the other one is screaming at you.

you can just have a drop-down menu pull the active market data including everything like implied volatility and all your other basics and get your ball park so you don't have to sit there and stare at your phone for 10 minutes. 

to back the above: for the people who use alpaca like i used to back in the day, if you have a brokerage account (tradier, schwab, tasty trade, whatever) and you are comfortable enough yourself with basic api functions but just don't feel like making it, just make your own algo options paper trader and be more accurate than alpaca is anyway. since your fill is probably going to be way better on there than it is in reality but by a long shot. 

anyway that's my adhd rant for the day. if you're interested, throw a comment here. if not, throw some hate here. i like it all. i'm not here to promote or sell anything. that would be sweet though... i'm not gonna lie, but honesty I dont need the money and I enjoy developing sh\\\\\\\*t.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
for someone on 24-hour shifts, a slippage diary. you feed it your broker's fill export plus the time each signal fired, and per trade it shows how far the price moved between the signal and the actual fill, split by time of day and by instrument.

reason I'd want it: almost everyone's backtest assumes the fill lands on the signal bar, and almost nobody checks how far off that is once it's live. on options it's usually the spread you crossed, on thin strikes at the open it can eat the whole edge, and you only find out by doing this by hand in a spreadsheet, which nobody with two kids and night shifts is going to do.

bonus if it flags the trades where the delay alone flipped a winner into a loser. that list tends to be short and very educational.

replies.author: sheehyct
replies.body:
Hah somewhat funny timing (also didn't think anyone would post a comment to this of something usually useful)

i was literally messing with this today. was scalping spx 0dte this morning and got annoyed at how much one it my contracts moved between click and fill, so i started messing around with it - at first from a latency standpoint due to some recent issues with Xfinity Internet at the firehouse. 

quick findings so far, just with stuff i already had lying around/could test on the fly, not what a final version would use/what you are requesting

- schwabs api gives you the time they received each order, the time of each fill, and where it got routed. so the "order in -> filled" gap is easy to pull. running that on today's trades after the close for the one SPX put that annoyed me a bit earlier. 
- tradingview with the opra add-on gives 1 min bars per option contract (looked here for cheap data people may already have vs something pricier)

So I pulled that one spx 0dte put from today and it traded 18.60 to 22.20 inside a single minute. thats like 18% in 60 seconds. so a few seconds of delay can eat a lot without anything actually being "slow"...this is where I currently settled with my own little experiment/latency thesis 

the hard part is exactly what you said. the math is nothing, its knowing the real bid/ask at the second the signal fired. for stocks, futures and perps thats easy and free. for options you pretty much have to record quotes live or pay for it, and yeah for someone like me with my life schedule your right. Spreadsheet isn't happening. 

so one version could do stocks/futures/perps properly, and options gets "where did your fill land inside that minute's range" until i sort out quote recording, but my assumption (what I think your getting at) is the others are easy to do...the options part isn't. I also have a feeling a one minute range isn't the level of accuracy you're looking for when comparing what slippage could do to a strategy and it's theoretical/potential edge. 

So few questions for you if you feel like answering ....is this mainly an options thing for you or do you trade other stuff too? Due to being busy trading options for me is more of a treat so I tend to trade perps/futures GTH hours.  

Where do your signal times come from, tradingview alerts, your own bot logs, something else? and which broker's fill export would you be feeding it? Obviously don't have to answer that, just info for me to take into account. 

also like the flipped winner to loser flag. thats just redoing the pnl with the signal price as the entry, so its trivial to add IMO

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
0dte is where that gap is worst, the quote can jump a few ticks in the half second between your click and the fill. logging signal time against fill time per contract shows it fast.

I built Quantradin this spring for the testing half: a buy fills on the quoted ask, a sell on the quoted bid, never the midpoint. quantradin.com

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Nice of you to share this, and the firehouse schedule makes the "must work fast on a phone" angle make sense. I agree with your point about paper trading, since fills at the mid price flatter every result, especially on wide option spreads. A paper trader that models the spread and some slippage is a great thing to share. Closing a position with biometrics from a watch is a smart touch too, because speed matters most when you only have a minute.
